name: Philosophy - BA - Mind, Brain, and Cognitive Sciences
narrative: A major in philosophy requires a total of fifteen philosophy courses, at least twelve of which must be upper-division (courses numbered 100 and above).

Up to two upper-division courses outside of philosophy can count among the twelve required for the major if they are drawn from a related field and contribute to the major's philosophical program; such credit must be approved by the undergraduate adviser.
Honors and directed study courses (PHIL 191–199) may not be used to satisfy the major requirement of fifteen philosophy courses.

Seven of the twelve upper-division courses in the major must be taken in the Department of Philosophy at UC San Diego. Courses taken at other institutions may be applied toward the major by petition only.
All courses applied toward the major must be taken for a letter grade and completed with a grade of C– or better. A GPA of 2.0 must be maintained in courses applied toward the major.

items.label: History of Philosophy
items.notes: These courses must be taken in order.

items.label: Upper-division philosophy courses
items.notes: Catalog: "a total of fifteen philosophy courses, at least twelve of which must be upper-division." The seven upper-division core courses and the three emphasis courses below count toward the twelve, so two more are needed here. A student whose core Metaphysics and Epistemology or Philosophy of Science course is not on the emphasis list takes the missing emphasis course(s) here. PHIL 191–199 may not be used. Up to two upper-division courses outside philosophy may count with adviser approval.

items.label: Remaining philosophy courses
items.notes: Fifteen philosophy courses in all: the eight core courses (including PHIL 10), the three emphasis courses and the two upper-division courses above count toward the fifteen; the remaining two may be lower- or upper-division.

sections.name: Area of Emphasis: Mind, Brain, and Cognitive Sciences

requirement.label: Mind, Brain, and Cognitive Sciences
requirement.notes: Catalog: "Students selecting an optional area of emphasis for the major must take and pass five of the courses listed under that area. Courses taken to complete an area of emphasis are counted toward the fifteen courses required for the major. Particular courses may be applied both to the completion of the area of emphasis and in fulfillment of a core requirement for the major." Five in all: the core Metaphysics and Epistemology course (if PHIL 132, 134 or 136) and Philosophy of Science course (if PHIL 145, 147, 149, 150 or 151) count toward the five, so three are listed here; if a core pick is not on this list, take another listed course in the upper-division group above. Areas of emphasis are not noted on transcripts or diplomas.
